summary: Defines the Link-Template HTTP header field, which describes the structure of a link between resources so that clients can generate new links from it. It is a template-based counterpart to the Link header field.

plainLanguage.summary: Link-Template lets an HTTP message provide a pattern for making links, rather than listing only fixed addresses. A client fills in values such as a username to create a link that fits its needs.

questions: how to describe url templates in http headers
how does link-template differ from link header
how do uri templates work in http headers
subtitle: An HTTP header that describes link patterns clients can expand into addresses.

tldr.problem: The Link header describes links with fixed targets, while clients sometimes need a pattern whose target depends on values they supply.
tldr.mechanism: Link-Template carries URI Templates in a Structured Field list. Parameters describe each link, and var-base can give template variables a shared base URI.
tldr.outcome: Clients can expand the templates to form links. RFC 9652 is a Proposed Standard and registers Link-Template as a permanent HTTP field.

today: RFC 9652 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Links That Can Be Filled In
sections.content: A URI Template becomes a URI when a set of variables is supplied. RFC 9652 defines an HTTP header field for sending these templates in message metadata. It complements the Link field, which carries links directly.
sections.plainLanguage: The server can send a link pattern with blanks instead of one fixed address. A client supplies values to make a link for a particular resource.

sections.title: The Link-Template Field
sections.content:
The field is a Structured Field list of strings. Each string contains a URI Template and may include parameters that describe the link. The rel and anchor parameters identify its relation and context; both must be strings, and anchor may itself be a template. Other target attributes use string values, or Display Strings when they contain non-ASCII characters.

For example, Link-Template: "/{username}"; rel="item" describes an item link whose target is made by expanding the username variable. Implementations must support all template levels defined by RFC 6570 in both the link string and the anchor parameter.
sections.plainLanguage: Each entry gives a pattern and notes about the link. For example, a client can put a username into a pattern to get that user's item link.

sections.title: Giving Template Variables a Base
sections.content:
The optional var-base parameter gives a base URI for resolving variable names in a template. This lets a variable have an identity that does not depend on where a particular link appears. A client resolves the variable against that base; if the result remains relative, it resolves it against the link context.

The RFC does not define what information a client might find by dereferencing a variable's URI.
sections.plainLanguage: var-base gives template variables a shared starting address. This helps different links use the same name for the same variable.

sections.title: Security and Registration
sections.content:
The security considerations for Link fields and URI Templates also apply here. Target attributes carried as Display Strings can be vulnerable to many kinds of attack. The RFC points to Unicode security guidance but does not give specific handling rules because use cases vary.

IANA added Link-Template to the HTTP Field Name Registry with Permanent status.
sections.plainLanguage: Display Strings can contain characters that create security problems, so implementations need to handle them carefully. The field name is registered for permanent use.
